title: AWL Sublist 1
description: Las 60 familias de palabras más frecuentes de la Academic Word List, imprescindibles para leer y escribir textos académicos.

cards.definition: To examine something in detail in order to understand it or explain it.
cards.example: The study analyses survey data from over 2,000 university students.
cards.note: Ortografía británica: analyse; americana: analyze. El plural de analysis es analyses.

cards.definition: A way of dealing with a problem or situation; to come nearer to something.
cards.example: A more holistic approach to public health could reduce long-term costs.
cards.warning: Se dice 'approach a problem' (sin 'to') pero 'an approach to the problem'. Nunca 'approach to solve': usa 'approach to solving'.

cards.definition: A part of a place, or a particular subject or field of activity.
cards.example: Rural areas often lack access to specialist medical services.

cards.definition: To judge the quality, size, value or importance of something.
cards.example: It is difficult to assess the long-term impact of social media on children.

cards.definition: To accept something as true without proof; to take on a role or responsibility.
cards.es: suponer, dar por hecho; asumir (un cargo)
cards.example: Many people assume that technology always improves productivity, but the evidence is mixed.
cards.warning: 'Asumir un error' no es 'assume a mistake' sino 'admit/accept a mistake'. 'Assume' significa sobre todo 'suponer'.

cards.definition: The power to give orders or make decisions; an official organisation; an expert.
cards.example: Local authorities are responsible for waste collection and recycling.

cards.definition: Able to be used, obtained or reached.
cards.example: Free online courses are now available to anyone with an internet connection.

cards.definition: An advantage or helpful effect; to be helped by something.
cards.example: Both employers and employees benefit from flexible working arrangements.
cards.warning: Es 'benefit from something', no 'benefit of something' como verbo. 'Beneficio' económico de una empresa suele ser 'profit'.

cards.definition: An abstract idea or principle.
cards.example: The concept of sustainability has become central to urban planning.

cards.definition: To be made of or formed from particular parts; to be based on.
cards.example: The committee consists of twelve members from different departments.
cards.warning: Nunca en forma continua: 'The test consists of', no 'is consisting of'. 'Consistent' significa 'coherente/constante', no 'consistente' (sólido).

cards.definition: To form or be the parts of something; to be considered as something.
cards.example: Women constitute nearly half of the global workforce.

cards.definition: The situation or background that helps explain an event or idea.
cards.example: These findings must be interpreted in the context of a changing labour market.

cards.definition: A formal written agreement; to make something smaller or to catch an illness.
cards.example: Many young workers are employed on short-term contracts with few benefits.
cards.warning: 'Contratar' a alguien es 'hire' o 'employ', no 'contract someone'.

cards.definition: To make something new or cause something to exist.
cards.example: Investment in renewable energy could create thousands of new jobs.

cards.definition: Facts or information, especially numbers, collected for analysis.
cards.example: The data suggest a strong link between sleep quality and exam performance.
cards.warning: En inglés académico 'data' es plural ('the data show'), aunque también se acepta singular. Nunca 'datas'.

cards.definition: To state or explain the exact meaning or limits of something.
cards.example: Poverty can be defined in both absolute and relative terms.

cards.definition: To get something from a particular source; to come from something.
cards.example: Much of the country's income is derived from tourism.
cards.warning: 'Derivar a alguien' (a un médico) es 'refer', no 'derive'.

cards.definition: To share or spread something among people or over an area.
cards.example: Wealth is distributed very unevenly in most developing economies.

cards.definition: The system by which a country produces and uses goods and money.
cards.example: Small businesses play a vital role in the local economy.
cards.warning: 'Economic' = relacionado con la economía; 'economical' = barato, que ahorra. 'Economic growth', pero 'an economical car'.

cards.definition: The natural world; also the conditions in which people live or work.
cards.example: Plastic waste poses a serious threat to the marine environment.

cards.definition: To start or create something that will last; to prove a fact.
cards.example: The university was established in 1890 to train engineers.

cards.definition: To guess a number or value based on available information; such a guess.
cards.example: It is estimated that 40% of food produced globally is wasted.
cards.warning: 'Estimar' a una persona (apreciar) es 'esteem' o 'value', no 'estimate'.

cards.definition: Clear and easy to see or understand.
cards.example: It is evident that public transport needs further investment.
cards.warning: 'Evidence' es incontable: 'a piece of evidence', nunca 'an evidence' ni 'evidences'.

cards.definition: To sell goods to another country; a product sold abroad.
cards.example: Coffee remains the country's main export.

cards.definition: One of the things that influences a result or situation.
cards.example: Cost is a key factor in deciding where students choose to study.

cards.definition: The management of money; to provide money for something.
cards.example: The project was financed by a combination of public and private funds.

cards.definition: A rule or method expressed in symbols; a fixed way of doing something.
cards.example: There is no simple formula for reducing traffic congestion.

cards.definition: The purpose of something; to work or operate in a particular way.
cards.example: One function of museums is to preserve cultural heritage.

cards.definition: To recognise or discover who or what someone or something is.
cards.example: Researchers have identified several causes of declining bee populations.

cards.definition: Money received regularly from work, investments or other sources.
cards.example: Households on a low income spend a larger share on food.
cards.warning: Ingresos altos/bajos: 'high/low income', no 'big/small income'.

cards.definition: To show or suggest that something is true or exists.
cards.example: Recent figures indicate a steady rise in online shopping.

cards.definition: A single person, considered separately from a group; relating to one person.
cards.example: Governments should protect individual freedom while promoting the common good.

cards.definition: To explain or decide the meaning of something; to translate spoken words.
cards.example: The same statistics can be interpreted in very different ways.
cards.warning: 'Interpretar' un papel en teatro es 'play a role', no 'interpret a role'.

cards.definition: To include something as a necessary part; to make someone take part.
cards.example: Learning a language involves a great deal of regular practice.
cards.warning: 'Involve' va con -ing: 'involves practising', no 'involves to practise'.

cards.definition: An important topic or problem for debate; to officially give or announce.
cards.example: Climate change is the most pressing issue of our time.

cards.definition: Work, especially physical work; workers considered as a group.
cards.example: Automation has reduced the demand for unskilled labour.
cards.warning: 'Labour' es trabajo (sobre todo físico) o mano de obra; para 'mi trabajo' o 'una labor/tarea' se usa 'work' o 'task', no 'labour'. En EE. UU. se escribe 'labor'.

cards.definition: Allowed by law, or connected with the law.
cards.example: Companies have a legal obligation to protect customer data.

cards.definition: To make laws.
cards.example: Several countries have legislated to ban single-use plastics.
cards.warning: 'Legislation' es incontable: 'a piece of legislation' o 'a law', no 'a legislation'.

cards.definition: Very large or important; a student's main subject at university (US).
cards.example: Air pollution is a major cause of respiratory disease in cities.
cards.warning: 'Major' no significa 'mayor' de edad o tamaño en general: 'older', 'bigger'. 'La mayoría de' = 'most' o 'the majority of'.

cards.definition: A particular way of doing something, especially a planned one.
cards.example: Traditional teaching methods are being replaced by interactive approaches.

cards.definition: To happen; to exist or be found somewhere.
cards.example: Most road accidents occur within a few kilometres of the driver's home.
cards.warning: Se dobla la r: occurred, occurring. 'Se me ocurrió' = 'It occurred to me', no 'I occurred'.

cards.definition: One part in every hundred.
cards.example: Approximately 30 percent of the respondents worked part-time.
cards.warning: 'Percent' va con número (30 percent); sin número se dice 'percentage': 'a high percentage', no 'a high percent'.

cards.definition: A length of time.
cards.example: Unemployment fell steadily over the period from 2010 to 2020.

cards.definition: A plan of action agreed by a government, organisation or person.
cards.example: The government introduced a policy to reduce car use in city centres.
cards.warning: 'Política' como actividad de partidos es 'politics'; una medida concreta es 'policy'.

cards.definition: A basic truth, rule or belief that guides behaviour or explains something.
cards.example: Equal pay for equal work is a fundamental principle of fairness.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'principal' (principal, director). 'Al principio' es 'at first' o 'at the beginning', no 'at principle'.

cards.definition: To continue doing something or move forward; to start an action.
cards.example: Once the funding was approved, the project proceeded quickly.
cards.warning: 'Proceder de' (venir de) se dice 'come from' o 'originate in', no 'proceed from' en uso normal.

cards.definition: A series of actions done to achieve a result; to deal with or treat something.
cards.example: The recycling process involves sorting, cleaning and melting the materials.

cards.definition: To need something; to make something necessary or compulsory.
cards.example: Most universities require international applicants to provide an IELTS score.

cards.definition: Detailed study to discover new facts or information.
cards.example: Recent research shows that bilingual children develop strong problem-solving skills.
cards.warning: 'Research' es incontable: 'a study' o 'some research', nunca 'a research' ni 'researches'. 'Investigar' un crimen = 'investigate'.

cards.definition: To say or do something as a reaction to something.
cards.example: Governments must respond quickly to public health emergencies.

cards.definition: The function or position someone or something has in a situation.
cards.example: Parents play a crucial role in their children's education.
cards.warning: Es 'play a role in', no 'have a paper in'. No confundir con 'roll' (rollo, rodar).

cards.definition: One of the parts into which something is divided.
cards.example: The final section of the report presents several recommendations.

cards.definition: A part of a country's economy or of an area of activity.
cards.example: The service sector now employs more than 70% of the workforce.

cards.definition: Important or large enough to have an effect or be noticed.
cards.example: There has been a significant increase in the number of remote workers.

cards.definition: Almost the same as something else, but not identical.
cards.example: The two countries have similar levels of income but very different health outcomes.
cards.warning: Es 'similar to', no 'similar than' ni 'similar of'.

cards.definition: The place or thing that something comes from; to obtain from a place.
cards.example: Solar power is becoming a cheaper source of energy than coal.

cards.definition: Particular or exact rather than general.
cards.example: Each student receives feedback on specific areas for improvement.

cards.definition: The way parts are arranged or organised; to organise something.
cards.example: A clear structure makes an essay much easier to follow.

cards.definition: A set of ideas that explains something; an idea not yet proven.
cards.example: In theory, higher taxes on sugar should reduce consumption.

cards.definition: To be different in different situations; to change.
cards.example: Attitudes towards remote work vary considerably between generations.
